blog_summary: The blog post introduces the FIT trade-off for distributed databases, which states that a system can have any two of Fairness, strong Isolation, and Throughput, but not all three. Adrian Colyer highlights that this challenges the common perception of an isolation-throughput trade-off by introducing fairness as a key variable. The paper argues that distributed coordination is unavoidable for distributed transactions, but systems can manage its cost by prioritizing or delaying transactions (fairness) rather than weakening isolation. The key insight is that strong isolation and high throughput are achievable if fairness is sacrificed, and vice versa. The post also clarifies the definitions of fairness, isolation, and the role of coordination in distributed transaction processing.
paper_title: FIT: A Distributed Database Performance Trade-off
paper_abstract: Designing distributed database systems is an inherently complex process, involving many choices and tradeoffs that must be considered. It is impossible to build a distributed database that has all the features that users intuitively desire. In this article, we discuss the three-way relationship between three such desirable features — fairness, isolation, and throughput (FIT) — and argue that only two out of the three of them can be achieved simultaneously.
